cleanIntro:
US Palm's own field strip for the Storm CAT4, rifle and pistol alike, in US Palm's order and no further. Every control is on both sides of the gun; the two receiver pins are drawn from the right.

US Palm gives no round count or schedule for cleaning. Its field strip goes all the way to the buffer and buffer spring; here those two are the deep clean.

steps.title: Magazine out first
steps.action: Point the muzzle in a safe direction, finger off the trigger, and keep it there. Press the magazine release on either side and pull the magazine out of the well.
steps.prose: Keep a hand under it: an unsupported magazine may drop free. With it out, working the charging handle cannot feed another round. A round already in the chamber is still there.
steps.quote: Remove the magazine from the firearm by pressing either of the ambidextrous magazine release buttons and pull the magazine to remove it from the lower receiver magwell.
steps.cite: US PALM STORM SERIES — OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Unloading & Clearing, printed p.19
steps.warn: THIS FIREARM WILL FIRE WITH THE MAGAZINE REMOVED IF THERE IS A CARTRIDGE IN THE CHAMBER AND THE TRIGGER IS PULLED.

steps.title: Charging handle all the way back, carrier locked there
steps.action: Pull the charging handle fully rearward and keep tension on it. While you hold it, set the bolt catch: lift the one on the right side, or press the lower paddle of the one on the left.
steps.prose: Watch the ejection port as the carrier comes back. Do not let go until you have felt the catch take the carrier; a half-set catch lets it slam shut.
steps.quote: Retract the charging handle fully to the rear and keep tension to hold the bolt carrier group to the rear.
steps.cite: US PALM STORM SERIES — OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Unloading & Clearing, steps 1–2, printed p.20

steps.title: Handle returned forward, selector on SAFE
steps.action: Push the charging handle forward until it latches on the upper receiver, then turn the selector to SAFE.
steps.prose: The selector comes this late for a reason: on this gun it turns to SAFE only with the hammer cocked, and pulling the carrier back has just cocked it.
steps.quote: Rotate the fire control selector to the “SAFE” position.
steps.cite: US PALM STORM SERIES — OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Unloading & Clearing, steps 3–4, printed p.20; Fire Control Selector, printed p.14

steps.title: Look: magazine well, bolt face, chamber
steps.action: With the ejection port cover open, the magazine out and the carrier locked back, look through the port into the chamber, then at the bolt face and into the magazine well. There must be no live round and no case in any of them.
steps.prose: The catch alone is holding the carrier against the buffer spring while you look. Keep hands and sleeves off it. If a case or round is stuck and will not come out, stop: US Palm says to store the gun away from its magazine with the safety on, and see a qualified gunsmith.
steps.quote: Carefully inspect the magazine well, bolt face and chamber to make sure there are no live rounds or cartridge cases present.
steps.cite: US PALM STORM SERIES — OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Unloading & Clearing, printed p.21; Stoppages & Malfunctions, printed p.22
steps.warn: DEPRESSING THE BOLT RELEASE ON LEFT OR RIGHT SIDE OF THE FIREARM WILL ALLOW THE BOLT CARRIER GROUP TO SPRING FORWARD AND COULD CAUSE INJURY.

steps.title: Safety glasses on, carrier forward on the empty chamber
steps.action: Put safety glasses on. With the gun proven empty, let the carrier go forward with the charging handle or with either bolt release.
steps.prose: Keep fingers out of the port; the carrier goes home under full spring force. It has to be forward before the receivers are opened.
steps.quote: Once firearm is unloaded and cleared utilize the charging handle or one of the ambidextrous bolt release levers to release the bolt carrier group forward into battery on the empty chamber.
steps.cite: US PALM STORM SERIES — OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Field Stripping, step 2, printed p.24
steps.warn: WEAR SAFETY GLASSES EVERY TIME YOU ASSEMBLE OR DISASSEMBLE YOUR FIREARM TO PROTECT YOUR EYES FROM SPRINGS OR OTHER PARTS.

steps.title: Takedown pin drawn out on the right until the detent holds it
steps.action: The takedown pin is the rear one. Draw it out on the right side of the gun until its detent catches it. It stays with the lower.
steps.prose: A tight pin is not a fault here: the anti-wobble tensioner in the lower loads it. US Palm allows a chamber flag, a wooden dowel that fits or a brass punch to start it. A steel punch may mar the finish.
steps.quote: Fully retract the takedown pin on the right side of the firearm until the detent engages the pin.
steps.cite: US PALM STORM SERIES — OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Field Stripping, step 3, printed p.24; Anti-Wobble Tensioning, printed p.36

steps.title: Upper swung open, carrier drawn back and out
steps.action: Swing the upper open on the pivot pin, which is the front one. Pull the charging handle back, which brings the bolt carrier group with it, and lift the group out of the rear of the upper.
steps.prose: Support the carrier as it clears the receiver so it does not drop. The handle stays in the upper for now.
steps.quote: Retract the charging handle which will move the bolt carrier group along with it to the rear.
steps.cite: US PALM STORM SERIES — OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Field Stripping, steps 4–6, printed p.25

steps.title: Charging handle out where its tabs meet the slots
steps.action: Move the charging handle along the upper until the tabs on its body sit at the slots in the receiver, and take it out there.
steps.prose: There is only one place along the track where it comes out. If it will not lift, the tabs are not at the slots; move it, do not pry.
steps.quote: Line up the tabs on the charging handle body with the slots in the upper receiver to remove the charging handle from the upper receiver.
steps.cite: US PALM STORM SERIES — OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Field Stripping, step 7, printed p.25

steps.title: Upper closed again, pivot pin drawn, receivers apart
steps.action: Swing the upper closed onto the lower. Draw the pivot pin out on the right side until its detent catches it, then separate the upper from the lower.
steps.prose: US Palm closes the receivers before the pivot pin is drawn. Keep hold of both halves: nothing joins them once this pin is out.
steps.quote: Fully retract the pivot pin on the right side of the firearm until the detent engages the pin.
steps.cite: US PALM STORM SERIES — OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Field Stripping, steps 8–10, printed p.26

steps.title: Firing pin retaining pin out, then the firing pin
steps.action: On the bolt carrier group, take out the firing pin retaining pin. Then take the firing pin out of the carrier.
steps.prose: The retaining pin is the only thing named as holding the firing pin, so it comes first. Put both somewhere they cannot roll.
steps.quote: Once the firing pin retaining pin is removed the firing pin can be removed from the bolt carrier.
steps.cite: US PALM STORM SERIES — OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Field Stripping, steps 11–12, printed p.27

steps.title: Bolt pushed in, cam pin a quarter turn and up
steps.action: Push the bolt face all the way into the carrier so the cam pin runs to the back of its path. Turn the cam pin 90 degrees, either way, and pull it up and out.
steps.prose: The quarter turn is what gets it past the gas key. If it will not lift, it is not turned far enough, or the bolt is not fully in.
steps.quote: Rotate the cam pin 90 degrees in either direction so that it can clear the gas key and pull up to remove it from the bolt carrier.
steps.cite: US PALM STORM SERIES — OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Field Stripping, step 13, printed p.27

steps.title: Bolt out of the carrier
steps.action: With the cam pin gone, draw the bolt out of the carrier.
steps.prose: Leave the bolt as it is. The book lists the extractor as a part and gives no procedure for taking it off.
steps.quote: Once the cam pin is removed the bolt can be removed from the carrier.
steps.cite: US PALM STORM SERIES — OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Field Stripping, step 14, printed p.27; parts list, printed p.39

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: You have the upper receiver with its barrel and handguard, the lower receiver, the charging handle, and the bolt carrier, bolt, cam pin, firing pin and retaining pin. The buffer and buffer spring are still in the lower; they are the deep clean.
steps.prose: Past what this book shows, US Palm recommends a gunsmith. Its warranty does not cover disassembly beyond these field stripping instructions.
steps.quote: It is recommended that any maintenance beyond what is contained in this manual be performed by a qualified gunsmith.
steps.cite: US PALM STORM SERIES — OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Safety, Rule #7, printed p.6; Limited Lifetime Warranty, printed p.41

steps.title: Chamber and bore with bore solvent, then dry
steps.action: Clean the chamber and the bore with a bore solvent and a rifle cleaning kit, following the kit maker’s own instructions. Patch the bore dry, and look through it before the gun is next fired.
steps.prose: US Palm wants solvent out of the barrel before firing, and puts the how of it in your kit’s instructions, not in this book. Work where there is air moving: some solvents give off hazardous vapor.
steps.quote: Clean the barrel chamber and bore with a quality bore solvent.
steps.cite: US PALM STORM SERIES — OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Cleaning and Maintenance, printed pp.29–30
steps.warn: Wipe the inside of the barrel dry before firing and ensure that it is free of obstructions.

steps.title: Carrier way in the upper, with no wire brush
steps.action: Clean the residue and carbon out of the carrier way, the track inside the upper that the bolt carrier runs in, with a solvent such as CLP. Wipe it, dry it and look it over, then put a thin film of lubricant on the surfaces the carrier bears on.
steps.prose: The upper is aluminum and its finish is anodized. A wire brush scratches through it, and that does not come back.
steps.quote: Bolt carrier interface (carrier way) in the upper receiver
steps.cite: US PALM STORM SERIES — OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Cleaning and Maintenance, item 1, printed p.30; Lubrication, item 1, printed p.31
steps.warn: USE OF WIRE BRUSHES ON ALUMINUM SURFACES CAN PERMANENTALLY SCRATCH OR MAR THE ANODIZED FINISH.

steps.title: Charging handle cleaned, film on its bearing surfaces
steps.action: Clean the charging handle with solvent, wipe it dry and look it over. Leave a thin film of lubricant where it bears on the upper receiver.
steps.prose: Only where it bears. Oil anywhere else on the handle just holds dirt.
steps.quote: Charging handle (apply a thin layer to the bearing surfaces of the upper receiver)
steps.cite: US PALM STORM SERIES — OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Cleaning and Maintenance, item 9, printed p.30; Lubrication, item 7, printed p.31

steps.title: Carrier, bolt, cam pin, firing pin and retaining pin cleaned
steps.action: Clean the residue and carbon off all five parts with a solvent such as CLP. Wipe each one, dry it and look it over before any lubricant goes on.
steps.prose: Dry and inspected first, lubricated second. Wear gloves: there may be sharp edges on these parts.
steps.quote: Clean parts listed with a quality solvent such as CLP then wipe, dry, and inspect prior to lubrication and re-assembly.
steps.cite: US PALM STORM SERIES — OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Cleaning and Maintenance, items 2–6, printed pp.29–30

steps.title: Carrier, bolt and cam pin lubricated; bolt face left dry
steps.action: Thin film on the carrier’s bearing surfaces. Thin film on the bolt’s bearing surfaces and the back of its lugs, none on the face. One or two drops on the cam pin.
steps.prose: The firing pin and its retaining pin are on US Palm’s cleaning list and not on its lubrication list. Leave them dry. Too much solvent or lubricant can upset how the gun runs.
steps.quote: Bolt (apply a thin layer to the bearing surfaces and rear of the lugs, do not lubricate the bolt face where the cartridge seats)
steps.cite: US PALM STORM SERIES — OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Lubrication, items 2–4, printed p.31; Cleaning and Maintenance, printed p.29

steps.title: Look it over while it is apart
steps.action: Look at every part for wear and damage before it goes back. Anything doubtful goes to a gunsmith before the gun is fired.
steps.prose: US Palm wants a competent gunsmith to check the gun now and then even when nothing looks wrong. It sets no interval for it.
steps.quote: This firearm should be checked periodically for worn or damaged parts by a competent gunsmith.
steps.cite: US PALM STORM SERIES — OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Cleaning and Maintenance, printed p.29

deepSteps.title: Buffer held, detent pressed, buffer let out slowly
deepSteps.action: Safety glasses on, upper off the lower. Keep a thumb on the face of the buffer, press the buffer detent down, and let the buffer and its spring come out of the tube under your thumb.
deepSteps.prose: The spring is pushing on the buffer the whole time and the detent is what stops it. Point the tube’s open end away from your face, and do not let go as it clears.
deepSteps.quote: Depress the buffer detent to allow the buffer and buffer spring to come out of the buffer tube.
deepSteps.cite: US PALM STORM SERIES — OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Field Stripping, step 15, printed p.28
deepSteps.warn: WEAR SAFETY GLASSES EVERY TIME YOU ASSEMBLE OR DISASSEMBLE YOUR FIREARM TO PROTECT YOUR EYES FROM SPRINGS OR OTHER PARTS.

deepSteps.title: Buffer and spring separated
deepSteps.action: Take the buffer off the buffer spring. US Palm’s strip ends here.
deepSteps.prose: The detent and the spring under it stay in the lower. The book gives no step for taking those out.
deepSteps.quote: This completes field stripping of the firearm.
deepSteps.cite: US PALM STORM SERIES — OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Field Stripping, steps 16–17, printed p.28

deepSteps.title: Buffer and buffer spring cleaned and dried
deepSteps.action: Clean the residue off the buffer and the spring with a solvent such as CLP. Wipe both, dry them, and look them over.
deepSteps.prose: These are the last two parts on US Palm’s cleaning list that the routine clean leaves in the gun.
deepSteps.quote: Clean the following items of any residue and/or carbon build up:
deepSteps.cite: US PALM STORM SERIES — OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Cleaning and Maintenance, items 7–8, printed p.30

deepSteps.title: Thin film on the buffer, light oil on the spring
deepSteps.action: Put a thin film of lubricant on the buffer’s bearing surfaces and lightly lubricate the spring.
deepSteps.prose: Light is the maker’s word for every part on its list. Use a product made for firearms and nothing else.
deepSteps.quote: Buffer (apply a thin layer to the bearing surfaces)
deepSteps.cite: US PALM STORM SERIES — OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Lubrication, items 5–6, printed p.31

cleaning.name: BORE AND UPPER RECEIVER
tasks: Chamber and bore: bore solvent, by your cleaning kit’s instructions
Bore wiped dry and clear of obstructions before firing
Carrier way in the upper: solvent, wiped, dried, inspected
Lube: thin film in the carrier way where the carrier bears
⛔ No wire brush on aluminum surfaces

cleaning.name: CHARGING HANDLE
tasks: Solvent, then wiped, dried and inspected
Lube: thin film where it bears on the upper

cleaning.name: BOLT CARRIER GROUP
tasks: Carrier, bolt, cam pin, firing pin, retaining pin: solvent, wiped, dried, inspected
Lube: thin film on the carrier’s bearing surfaces
Lube: thin film on the bolt’s bearing surfaces and the back of its lugs
Lube: one or two drops on the cam pin
⛔ No lubricant on the bolt face where the cartridge seats
⛔ No lubricant sprayed or wiped on ammunition

reassembly: Safety glasses on. Buffer back onto the buffer spring, and both into the buffer tube.
⛔ Buffer pushed fully into the tube, past the buffer detent, so the detent captures it. Check that it stays captured when you let go.

⛔ Cam pin into the carrier and turned 90 degrees, with the bolt pushed in. Do not forget it: US Palm warns that the gun will still fire a round without its cam pin, and that firing it that way could end in catastrophic failure, serious injury or death.
Firing pin into the carrier, then the firing pin retaining pin.
Upper set on the lower, and the pivot pin pushed home.
Upper swung open on the pivot pin. Charging handle in, its tabs through the slots in the upper.
Bolt carrier group into the upper, and the group and charging handle pushed forward together.
Upper swung closed and the takedown pin pushed home. A dowel or brass punch helps if the tensioner makes it tight; a steel punch may mar the finish.
Function check before any live ammunition.
fncheck: Gun unloaded and proven clear first, muzzle in a safe direction throughout. Insert an EMPTY magazine until its catch holds it. Pull the charging handle fully back: the empty magazine should lift the bolt catch and lock the carrier back. Push the handle forward until it latches, and turn the selector to SAFE. Take the magazine out. Let the carrier forward with the right bolt release or the top paddle of the left one. Press the trigger: the hammer should NOT fall. Turn the selector to SEMI, then press the trigger and hold it back: the hammer should fall. Still holding the trigger back, pull the charging handle fully rearward to reset the hammer. Let the trigger go: you should hear it click as it resets. Turn the selector to SAFE. If the gun fails any part of this, do not load it; take it to a qualified gunsmith.
reassemblyRoutine: Safety glasses on. Bolt into the bolt carrier.

⛔ Cam pin into the carrier and turned 90 degrees, with the bolt pushed in. Do not forget it: US Palm warns that the gun will still fire a round without its cam pin, and that firing it that way could end in catastrophic failure, serious injury or death.

Upper set on the lower, and the pivot pin pushed home.
Upper swung open on the pivot pin. Charging handle in, its tabs through the slots in the upper.
Bolt carrier group into the upper, and the group and charging handle pushed forward together.
Upper swung closed and the takedown pin pushed home. A dowel or brass punch helps if the tensioner makes it tight; a steel punch may mar the finish.
